clue.text: Servant is not from the factory, we hear

indicators.note: the clue tells us the phrase is something heard spoken rather than read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: goods not from a factory are made by hand, hand-made

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a servant is a person of humble, non-industrial origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals a sound-alike: HAND-MADE, what something not from the factory is, is pronounced like the servant's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid serving a lady is an old word for a female attendant or servant.

clue.text: Frosty type, the German storekeeper

parts.note: hoar is a white frost
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A cold, unfriendly German runs a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stockpiles or keeps a store of things hidden away.

clue.text: Is money such an evil ?

parts.note: plays on the saying that money is the root of all evil, and on the phrase for something bad but unavoidable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether cash is really so wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the love of money is the root of all evil; the answer completes the phrase for an unavoidable bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bad but unavoidable is called an indispensable evil.

clue.text: Acclaiming, as the crowd the crooner

definitions.text: Acclaiming, as the crowd the crooner

parts.words: Acclaiming, as the crowd the crooner
parts.note: fans surging around a popular singer to cheer him

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers a popular singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowding around someone in a disorderly throng, as fans do with a pop star.

clue.text: The British, so parochial

definitions.meaning: as islanders, the British are inhabitants of an island nation

explanation.definitionFit: Describing island-dwellers, and narrow-minded in outlook as islanders were thought to be.

clue.text: Sundry frogmen

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning various or several

explanation.definitionFit: The old adjective for various shares its spelling with the plural of the word for underwater swimmers.

clue.text: Divert pay? It's organized corruption

indicators.note: the letters are organized, put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Misappropriating wages is a systematic racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' looks like part of 'organized corruption', organized crime; it signals the anagram of DIVERT PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral wickedness or debasement is corruption of character.

clue.text: Stoker character in Sussex? Holmes investigated

definitions.meaning: Bram Stoker wrote the novel Dracula
Conan Doyle's story about the Sussex blood-sucker, a case for Sherlock Holmes

explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the bloodsucking count of Bram Stoker's novel, and a Sherlock Holmes case title mentions one in Sussex, an English county.

clue.text: Concerning magistrate, or oil-man

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a magistrate fines offenders, so is one who fines

explanation.surface: Asks about whether a judge or petrol tycoon is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: One who works at purifying crude petroleum into oil products.

clue.text: Temple not his habitual place of worship

definitions.text: Temple not his habitual place of worship

parts.words: Temple not his habitual place of worship
parts.note: Temple is the surname of William Temple, a famous churchman, whose usual place of worship would be a cathedral rather than a temple

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a temple is not where a certain person normally prays.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick and William Temple were both Archbishops of Canterbury; the capital T hides a surname behind the building.
explanation.definitionFit: William Temple held the senior post of Primate of All England, head of the English church.

clue.text: Failure to catch a woman's fur

definitions.meaning: to fumble or drop a ball in a game, a dropped catch
a tube of fur for warming the hands

explanation.definitionFit: A dropped catch in cricket is a fumble, and the same word names a fur hand-warmer.

clue.text: "Play up, lads!" Net with him in charge

definitions.text: "Play up, lads!" Net with him in charge

parts.words: "Play up, lads!" Net with him in charge
parts.note: a schoolmaster shouting encouragement at cricket nets, a strict figure who keeps the boys in order

explanation.surface: A master urges boys on at cricket practice in the nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play up' could mean misbehave as well as play hard; with a strict master in charge of the nets, there is no misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict enforcer of order and rules, such as a stern schoolmaster.

clue.text: Genuine fish used in making fireworks

definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase for a substance rather than a noun

parts.note: genuine means real
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: An authentic fish is somehow an ingredient of fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: This red arsenic sulphide mineral was traditionally used in pyrotechnics for its white flame.

clue.text: The aim of the Duchess's little boy's sneezes

definitions.text: The aim of the Duchess's little boy's sneezes

parts.words: The aim of the Duchess's little boy's sneezes
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Duchess sings that the little boy sneezes only to irritate

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a noblewoman's child keeps sneezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess's lullaby: 'Speak roughly to your little boy... He only does it to annoy, Because he knows it teases.'
explanation.definitionFit: Causing irritation or vexation is the stated purpose of the boy's sneezes.

clue.text: Sack member, for producing a gun ?

parts.note: to sack a worker is to fire them
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Dismissing a club member somehow leads to a weapon appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Any portable weapon such as a pistol or rifle is a gun.

clue.text: A couple of gins — so extremely distressing!

indicators.note: extremely is read as wildly or to an extreme degree, so the letters are scrambled
a couple means two, so the gin appears twice

parts.note: gin is the spirit

explanation.surface: Downing two gins proves terribly upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'distressing' but works on A, GIN, GIN, SO as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing great pain or anguish, harrowing.

clue.text: Pepper at opposite ends of kitchen, say

indicators.note: the letters at either end are to be spoken by their names, so sound is wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of kitchen are K and N, spoken as kay and en

explanation.surface: Peppers are kept at either end of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for the letter names: K and N spoken aloud make kay-en, roughly the sound of the hot pepper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot red chilli powder named after the capital of French Guiana.

clue.text: Mostly tropical variety of fruit

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Most of these fruits are a tropical kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final L of TROPICAL to give TROPICA, and 'variety of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small orange stone fruit related to the plum and peach.

clue.text: Save king imprisoned in passage

indicators.note: the king is locked up inside the other word

parts.note: save means except, as in all save one
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone tries to rescue a monarch held in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' is not rescue but the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an extract quoted from a book or piece of music.

clue.text: Old one-eyed Sicilian

parts.note: Greek legend placed the one-eyed giant Polyphemus and his kin on Sicily

explanation.surface: An elderly Sicilian has lost an eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer's Odysseus met the one-eyed giants on an island later identified with Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary giants with a single eye in mid-forehead, Polyphemus among them, of Greek myth.

clue.text: Messenger from the French court? That's right

parts.note: cour is French for court
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A messenger arrives from the French court, and someone confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who carries messages or packages, a dispatch rider.

clue.text: Henry Morgan's means to snub a girl?

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase for a weapon rather than a plain noun

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them, ignore them pointedly
lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A pirate captain's way of ignoring a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Morgan was a 17th-century Welsh privateer in the Caribbean; the pirate's short curved sword is his means.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved sword was the typical weapon of sailors and buccaneers.

clue.text: Hold up the sentence on Haman

definitions.meaning: to delay or put off temporarily
in the Book of Esther, Haman is hanged on the gallows he built

explanation.definitionFit: To halt temporarily or defer, and to hang from above, as the Biblical villain Haman was hanged.

clue.text: The heights of unsteadiness?

parts.note: wobbly or shaky is rocky, and heights are mountains, so these would be the peaks of shakiness

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the extremes of wobbliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heights' looks like an abstract peak of something; read literally it is a mountain range in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: A major range of peaks running through western North America whose name also suggests shakiness.

clue.text: Mark or Cliff?

definitions.meaning: a blemish such as the trace left by a healed wound
a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside

explanation.definitionFit: A healed wound's trace and a steep rock face share one spelling.

clue.text: Subject in this case to vote in main assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the preceding letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An election in a large meeting is the topic in this instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like the parliament; it is the anagram signal on VOTE IN MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the subject of a verb takes this case in languages like Latin.

clue.text: One may be cast — in "Don Giovanni" perhaps

definitions.text: One may be cast — in "Don Giovanni" perhaps

parts.words: One may be cast — in "Don Giovanni" perhaps
parts.note: cast reads as a casting for a role, but in bronze a figure is cast; Mozart's opera has a stone Commendatore who comes to life

explanation.surface: Someone may be given a role in a Mozart opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In Don Giovanni the murdered Commendatore returns as a stone figure from his tomb, so this cast object is also a part in the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted figure, often of bronze, made in a mould.

clue.text: Portended before the French painter's return

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the painter's name comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: A French artist's homecoming was foretold in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' looks like LE or LA, but here it just introduces the painter Degas; 'return' signals he is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow a future event is to foretell or portend it.
